questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit Using the Limit Definition of Euler's Number
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the following special limit: 

$$
e={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{n}
$$

Now, we rewrite the given limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{-20n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{[{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{n}]}^{-20} \\  & ={[{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{n}]}^{-20} \\  & ={e}^{-20} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{20}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Applying the Limit Definition of the Exponential Function
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the following special limit:

$$
{e}^{u}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{u}{n})}^{n}
$$

Hence, with $u=x\sqrt{2},$ we get

$$
{e}^{x\sqrt{2}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{x\sqrt{2}}{n})}^{n}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the given limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{x\sqrt{2}}{n})}^{n\sqrt{2}} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{[{(1+\frac{x\sqrt{2}}{n})}^{n}]}^{\sqrt{2}} \\  & ={[{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{x\sqrt{2}}{n})}^{n}]}^{\sqrt{2}} \\  & ={({e}^{x\sqrt{2}})}^{\sqrt{2}} \\  & ={e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$
